components: 32 built-in tools (read, write, edit, ast_edit, search, bash, eval, lsp, debug, task, browser, web_search)
14 LSP operations (diagnostics, navigation, symbols, renames, code actions)
28 DAP operations (breakpoints, stepping, threads, stack, variables)
2 persistent kernels (Python and Bun) with tool re-entry
first-class subagents with typed JSON results and IRC coordination
40+ LLM providers with per-role routing (default, smol, slow, plan)
architecture_facts: Every edit is anchored to a content hash of the surrounding code, not to a line number
An edit lands on the exact content it targets, or it is rejected rather than applied to the wrong place
Two parallel agents editing one file collide immediately by hash instead of silently corrupting it
Symbol operations like rename and find-callers go through the language server, not the model's text substitution
A built-in debugger drives real breakpoints and stepping through DAP
Persistent Python and Bun kernels can call back into the agent's own tools over a loopback bridge
It routes across 40+ providers with per-role routing for default, smol, slow, and plan roles
Native bindings for ripgrep and glob avoid fork and exec overhead
surprising_detail: Every edit is anchored to a content hash of the code around it, so the agent edits by what the code is rather than where it sits. A stale or conflicting edit is caught and rejected instead of quietly corrupting the file.
notes: Fork of pi-mono by Mario Zechner (https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono), extended into a batteries-included terminal coding agent. Tagline: 'A coding agent with the IDE wired in.' Repo README: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/main/README.md
